IN RE: JOHN L & VONETTA SMITH JR
PETITION FOR Review of Refund for Personal Income Tax
PERIOD(S) 2008
AND NOW, May 20, 2014, pursuant to the Fiscal Code, the Act of 1929, April 9, P.L. 343,
as amended, (72 P.S. § 1 et seq), the Board of Finance and Revenue of the Commonwealth of
Pennsylvania, based upon the reasons set forth herein, hereby ORDERS the following:
Jurisdiction
This petition comes before the Board of Finance and Revenue pursuant to Section 2704
of the Tax Reform Code of 1971, as amended, 72 P.S. § 9704.
Issue
Whether Petitioners were improperly assessed tax, penalties and interest on income
earned in New Jersey.
Statement of the Case
Petitioners, John L. and Vonetta Smith Jr., file the instant matter at the Board of Finance
and Revenue claiming that the tax which they were assessed by the Department of Revenue
for the 2008 tax year was withheld to New Jersey by Mr. Smith’s employer. Petitioners were
Pennsylvania residents earning income in New Jersey. The Department assessed Petitioners
on $ of compensation, and a tax liability of $ . The Department issued an
assessment notice on December 11, 2009, for the outstanding tax, plus penalties and interest.
Petitioners filed an appeal at the Board of Appeals (“BOA”) claiming that the
assessment was made in error because Mr. Smith had paid tax through his employer’s
withholding to New Jersey. In its Decision and Order dated November 21, 2013, the BOA
denied the petition, finding that Petitioners had not submitted evidence to support their appeal.
Petitioners file the instant matter at the Board of Finance and Revenue arguing that they
should not be penalized for Mr. Smith’s employer’s failure to properly withhold tax to

Pennsylvania in accordance with the reciprocal agreement between New Jersey and
Pennsylvania. Petitioners states that Mr. Smith requested that his employer withhold
Pennsylvania taxes, but that his request was refused. Department records show that
Petitioners had a total of $ of taxes withheld to New Jersey from their compensation.
Statement of the Law
Pennsylvania has entered into reciprocal agreements with Indiana, Maryland, New
Jersey, Ohio, Virginia, and West Virginia. Personal Income Tax Guide, 7-15 (Revised
February 2007), see also, Pa. Dept. of Revenue Ltr. Rul. PIT-05-016 (July 26, 2005).
Pennsylvania residents must have Pennsylvania taxes withheld on compensation, subject to
federal withholding, earned in reciprocal agreement states. Id. Residents of the reciprocal
agreement states working in Pennsylvania must have their home state’s taxes withheld on
compensation, subject to federal withholding, earned in Pennsylvania. Id.
Upon the filing of a petition for reassessment or a petition for refund as provided under
this act by a taxpayer, additions or penalties imposed upon the taxpayer by the laws of this
Commonwealth may be waived or abated, in whole or in part, where the petitioner has
established that he has acted in good faith, without negligence and with no intent to defraud.
72 P.S. § 9706.
Except as otherwise provided by this act, in all cases of petitions filed pursuant to this
article, the burden of proof shall be upon the petitioner or appellant, as the case may be.
72 P.S. § 9705.
Conclusion
Petitioners’ request for relief is granted in part.
Petitioners’ request to abate the assessed tax is denied. Pennsylvania residents must
have Pennsylvania taxes withheld on compensation, subject to federal withholding, earned in
reciprocal agreement states. Personal Income Tax Guide, 7-15 (Revised February 2007).
Petitioners are Pennsylvania residents working in New Jersey. Their Forms W-2 show that
taxes were withheld to New Jersey, instead of Pennsylvania as required by the reciprocal
agreement between the states. Petitioners have not provided sufficient evidence to establish
that the Department’s assessment was in error.
Petitioners’ request to abate penalties is granted. Penalties imposed upon the taxpayer
by the laws of this Commonwealth may be waived or abated, in whole or in part, where the
petitioner has established that he has acted in good faith, without negligence and with no intent
to defraud. 72 P.S. § 9706. Petitioners have established that they acted in good faith by
requesting Mr. Smith’s employer withhold his taxes to Pennsylvania. The fact that this request
was refused does not disqualify Petitioners from penalty abatement.
Interest is charged to compensate the Commonwealth for the loss of the use of the
funds while the tax shown to have been properly due is in the possession of the taxpayer.
Therefore, Petitioners’ request for abatement of interest must be denied for 2008.
